title: Microsoft ships own coding models, with cyber rollout set for December
headline: Microsoft releases new MAI coding models via GitHub Copilot
summary: Microsoft has introduced two new proprietary coding models, MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, alongside a cybersecurity model, MAI Cyber 2 Flash. The release expands Microsoft's role into building more underlying intelligence for platforms like GitHub Copilot. However, the deployment introduces complex purchasing, data-location, and governance decisions for enterprise buyers due to promotional pricing timelines, default model-enablement settings, and region-specific inference limitations.
why_it_matters: Australian compliance and procurement teams must verify actual AI data residency and control model-enablement settings rather than assuming local repository storage guarantees Australian AI inference.

quotes.text: Microsoft has released two new proprietary coding models through GitHub Copilot and outlined a December rollout for its latest cybersecurity model, expanding its role from supplying enterprise AI platforms to building more of the intelligence inside them.
Australian repository storage therefore should not be read as a guarantee of Australian AI inference.

Business and Enterprise administrators can control access through model policies. GitHub says new models are automatically enabled under its default model-enablement setting unless administrators have changed that setting or disabled the model.

dates_mentioned.quote: GitHub plans to retire MAI-Code-1.1-Flash on 18 December 2026 .
The promotion ends on 17 May 2027, when those rates are scheduled to double.

classification.significance_reason: Introduces new proprietary enterprise coding and security models with important data residency and default-enablement considerations for Australian buyers, but represents a product release rather than a new regulatory or legal obligation.
